title: Service dependability collab sprint map and decision log - Nov 2026
content:
Purpose

A concise cross-functional sprint map for operationalizing service dependability (SLOs + runbooks + rollout policy) across product, serving-runtime, infra, and observability teams. This doc is intentionally tactical — we want a concrete set of sprints, clear owners for decisions, and an embedded decision log so we avoid re-litigating choices.

Scope
- Services in phase 1: hosted API (generation/chat), embeddings, and routing layer (smart routing).
- Outcomes: (1) agreed SLOs + measurement windows; (2) automated alerting + burn dashboards; (3) canary + fallback playbook; (4) documented runbooks for top-5 incident classes; (5) a light-weight ops handoff for product on-call.
- Out of scope: private on-prem installs (follow-up Q1 2027 cadence).

High-level success criteria (what we will ship)
- SLO definitions pushed to telemetry and visible in Console per route/model within 28-day rolling windows.
- Error-budget policy enforced: automated mitigation actions at 25%/50%/90% burn.
- Canary gating for model rollouts: automatic pause/fallback if p95 or error rate violates threshold for > 5 mins.
- Runbooks for top-5 incident types with post-incident actionable items.

Core stakeholders + RACI (working names)
- Eng-SRE (Claire Zhang) - overall program lead / triage owner.
- Serving-runtime (Diego Ramos) - feasibility & kernel-level mitigation (batching / kv-cache).
- Infra (Jonas Meyer) - capacity / autoscaling / dedicated capacity policy changes.
- Observability (Aisha Patel) - metrics, dashboards, alerting, retention policies.
- Product - Hosted API (Priya Rao) - product acceptance, customer-facing SLAs and comms.
- Solutions / CS - (Michael O'Neil) - customer impact analysis, messaging.

Sprint map (6 sprints of 2 weeks) - target: Nov 2026 -> Feb 2027
Sprint 0 (Nov 16 - Nov 29) - Discovery + alignment
- Kickoff workshop: agree SLO measurement primitives (latency histograms, success/error tags, request classification by route/model).
- Audit: where are current gaps? (missing latency histograms for embeddings, inconsistent success tags for some retries).
- Deliverable: SLO spec doc (single page) + data quality checklist.

Sprint 1 (Nov 30 - Dec 13) - Measurement plumbing
- Observability to add/standardize metrics (p50, p95, p99 latency; availability/error-rate by route and model).
- Tagging conventions: env, tenant, model_version, route_id.
- Deliverable: dashboards + 28-day rolling SLO query templates; baseline numbers populated.

Sprint 2 (Dec 14 - Dec 27) - Alerting and burn policy ops
- Implement error-budget burn calculation (28-day rolling, with 1-day lookback) in Console.
- Alerts at burn thresholds: 25% (ops FYI), 50% (eng leadership review), 90% (urgent mitigation).
- Deliverable: burn alert config + playbook stub.

Sprint 3 (Jan 4 - Jan 17) - Runbooks + incident playbook
- Create runbooks for top-5 failure modes: (1) model OOMs / eviction; (2) high tail latency from streaming; (3) routing fallback storms; (4) datastore latency causing token-generation timeouts; (5) auth/token-throttling regressions.
- Tabletop run: run simulated incident with product & CS to validate comms.
- Deliverable: editable runbooks in shared drive + tabletop notes.

Sprint 4 (Jan 18 - Jan 31) - Canary/rollout automation
- Implement canary gating rules tied to SLO checks for model rollout pipeline: automatic rollback or traffic-shift to fallback model for violations >5m.
- Add smoke-run checks (small prompt set) executed during rollout.
- Deliverable: rollout gating policy + example rollout pipeline (docs + Jenkins/GitHub actions snippet).

Sprint 5 (Feb 1 - Feb 14) - Operational handoff & finish
- Finalize on-call runbooks + escalation matrix; ensure CS/product have incident messaging templates.
- Post-deploy review checklist and SLA publication plan for hosted API.
- Deliverable: SLA brief + go-to-customer comm plan.

Measurement & SLO examples (proposed canonical formats)
- Availability SLO (Gold routes): 99.95% success rate (success defined as 2xx and non-empty generation tokens) over a 28-day rolling window. Error budget: 0.05% * 28d.
- Latency SLO (interactive chat): p95 < 250ms server-side tail for requests <= 512 tokens (measured server processing time excluding network egress).
- Embeddings SLO: p95 < 150ms for batch size 1; availability 99.9.
- Degradation tolerance: For background / batch endpoints we allow a lower bar (availability 99.5) and a cost-latency tradeoff path.

Measurement details / gotchas
- Use rolling windows (28d) for consumer-facing SLOs; use short windows (1d) for canary gating.
- Normalize retries: metric should include first-attempt failures; buried retries can mask issues. Standardize exponent/backoff into a retry_tag.
- Distinguish client timeouts vs server errors (we should not count client-enforced timeouts against server SLO). TODO: telemetry event to mark client-cancelled requests.

Burn policy & automated responses (sketch)
- Burn 25%: annotate incident & notify product / infra (slack #sre-service-dependability).
- Burn 50%: reduce non-critical batch jobs, temporarily increase capacity on Dedicated pools (infra autonomy call).
- Burn 90%: disable lower-tier routes (background embeddings), throttle non-paid test traffic, initiate canary rollback pattern.

Canary and rollback criteria (practical rules)
- Canary window: 10-minute steady state check using both synthetic smoke prompts + real traffic sampling (1%).
- Abort if p95 increases >20% baseline OR availability drops >0.02% absolute during the check window.
- Automatic fallback: route to last-known-good model variant and trigger post-mortem.

Decision log (living)
- 2026-10-20: Agreed canonical rolling window = 28 days (owner: Aisha). Rationale: aligns with customer billing cycles and smoothing.
- 2026-10-27: Choose p95 for latency SLO (owner: Diego). Rationale: p99 too noisy; p95 matches customer-facing interactivity expectations.
- 2026-11-01: Canary abort thresholds: p95 +20% or availability -0.02% within 10m (owner: Claire). Rationale: conservative but avoids noisy rollback.

Open questions / TODOs (prioritized)
- [P0] How to tag out-of-band retries vs client-initiated retries? (Diego to propose telemetry change by Nov 30).
- [P0] Exact definition of "success" for multimodal outputs (images + text) — product to propose canonical success metric.
- [P1] Cost limits for automated scale-ups under 50% burn – should infra require approval? (Jonas to propose threshold).
- [P2] Retention policy for SLO telemetry: 90 days full resolution, then 365d summarized. Observability to draft.

Risk register (short)
- Risk: Measurement gaps cause false positives in burn alerts. Mitigation: phased rollout of alerts (observe for 2 weeks before action automation).
- Risk: Automated rollback during peak may cause customer-visible thrash. Mitigation: canary sampling + gradual traffic shifting before full rollback.
- Risk: Ops overhead for many teams if alerts are noisy. Mitigation: invest in metric hygiene and anomaly suppression heuristics.

Comms plan
- Weekly sync (30m) during sprints — Claire runs; rotate notes.
- Bi-weekly stakeholder demo (show dashboards + canary logs) for Eng leadership and product.
- Customer-facing SLA draft to be shared with sales/CS for feedback before public posting.

Artifacts to produce (checklist)
- SLO spec (single page) - obs + product signoff.
- Burn dashboard & alert configs - obs delivered.
- Top-5 runbooks - SRE + product review.
- Canary gating policy - serving-runtime + infra.
- Incident comm templates - CS + product.

Jira tags / example tickets (starter list)
- JIRA-OPS-10101: Add p95 latency histogram for embeddings pipeline
- JIRA-OBS-10102: Create burn calculation pipeline and dashboard
- JIRA-RUNTIME-10103: Add canary smoke-run for model rollout infra

Appendix: quick checklist for first incident exercise
1) Trigger tabletop for "routing fallback storm" scenario. 2) Execute comms template to CS with placeholders. 3) Validate runbook steps and mark missing steps as actions. 4) Update decision log.

Notes to self / informal
- Keep the SLO wording short and copyable to Console UI (customers hate long paragraphs).
- When in doubt, prefer progressive automation (alert -> manual -> auto-mitigate).
- We should capture a short video demo of the canary gating flow for non-technical stakeholders.
